_readme: Settings for scripts/build-seo-engine.mjs. coingeckoIds maps registry tickers (assets/coins.js) to CoinGecko ids; an asset without an id here gets no quant section. sectors: registry sector keys and/or explicit tickers. comparisons: curated pairs in priority order (the first 25 with data are built). references: one protocol fact per asset with its named primary source; assets without one cite only the market-data and methodology sources.

sectors.name: Layer 1
sectors.about: native assets of base-layer blockchains that settle their own transactions

sectors.name: Decentralized Finance
sectors.about: tokens of on-chain exchanges, lending markets, staking and derivatives protocols

sectors.name: AI & Compute
sectors.about: tokens of networks that coordinate machine-learning work, GPU compute, agents or data

sectors.name: Layer 2
sectors.about: tokens of rollups and other networks that execute transactions off a base chain and settle to it

sectors.name: Payments
sectors.about: assets designed mainly as a medium of exchange for peer-to-peer or cross-border transfers

sectors.name: Memecoins
sectors.about: community-driven tokens whose demand comes mainly from culture and attention rather than protocol fees

BTC.fact: the block subsidy halves every 210,000 blocks, which limits total issuance to just under 21 million BTC
BTC.source: Bitcoin whitepaper (Nakamoto, 2008) and the Bitcoin Core consensus rules

ETH.fact: there is no fixed maximum supply: a base fee is burned in every block under EIP-1559 and new ETH is issued only to proof-of-stake validators since the Merge of September 2022
ETH.source: Ethereum Improvement Proposal 1559 and the ethereum.org protocol documentation

BNB.fact: the Auto-Burn mechanism removes BNB from supply each quarter toward a stated target of 100 million BNB

XRP.fact: all 100 billion XRP were created when the XRP Ledger launched in 2012, no new XRP can be issued, and a small amount is destroyed with every transaction fee

SOL.fact: transactions are ordered with Proof of History alongside proof-of-stake, and the inflation rate started at 8% a year and declines 15% annually toward a 1.5% long-term rate
SOL.source: Solana whitepaper (Yakovenko) and the Solana documentation

DOGE.fact: each block pays a fixed 10,000 DOGE, about 5 billion new DOGE a year, and there is no maximum supply

ADA.fact: the Ouroboros proof-of-stake protocol secures the chain and the maximum supply is fixed at 45 billion ADA
ADA.source: Ouroboros paper (Kiayias et al., 2017) and the Cardano documentation

TRX.fact: blocks are produced by 27 elected Super Representatives under delegated proof-of-stake

LINK.fact: the total supply is fixed at 1 billion LINK

XLM.fact: the network reaches agreement with the Stellar Consensus Protocol, and the Stellar Development Foundation burned about 55 billion XLM in November 2019, leaving roughly 50 billion in existence
XLM.source: Stellar Consensus Protocol paper (Mazières, 2015) and the Stellar Development Foundation

BCH.fact: the 21 million coin limit and four-year halving schedule were inherited from Bitcoin at the August 2017 fork

LTC.fact: supply is capped at 84 million LTC, with the block reward halving every 840,000 blocks under Scrypt proof-of-work

AVAX.fact: supply is capped at 720 million AVAX and transaction fees are burned
AVAX.source: Avalanche platform whitepaper and Avalanche documentation

SUI.fact: total supply is capped at 10 billion SUI

HBAR.fact: the hashgraph consensus algorithm orders transactions and the total supply is fixed at 50 billion HBAR

SHIB.fact: SHIB is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum that launched with a supply of 1 quadrillion tokens
SHIB.source: Shiba Inu ecosystem documentation and the Ethereum ERC-20 standard (EIP-20)

NEAR.fact: the chain is sharded with the Nightshade design under proof-of-stake

UNI.fact: 1 billion UNI were minted at genesis in September 2020

DOT.fact: validators are selected through nominated proof-of-stake

XMR.fact: mining uses the RandomX proof-of-work algorithm and a tail emission of 0.6 XMR per block has applied since 2022

ZEC.fact: supply is capped at 21 million ZEC and shielded transactions rely on zk-SNARK proofs

ETC.fact: the ECIP-1017 monetary policy limits supply to about 210.7 million ETC

TAO.fact: supply is capped at 21 million TAO with periodic halvings of issuance

PEPE.fact: PEPE is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum with a total supply of 420.69 trillion tokens
PEPE.source: PEPE token contract and the Ethereum ERC-20 standard (EIP-20)

ATOM.fact: the Cosmos Hub runs CometBFT (formerly Tendermint) proof-of-stake consensus and ATOM has no maximum supply

FIL.fact: maximum supply is 2 billion FIL and storage providers are verified with proof-of-replication and proof-of-spacetime

ARB.fact: the token launched with an initial supply of 10 billion ARB and governs the Arbitrum optimistic rollups

POL.fact: POL replaced MATIC through a one-to-one migration with an initial supply of 10 billion

ALGO.fact: supply is capped at 10 billion ALGO under pure proof-of-stake

KAS.fact: blocks are ordered with the GHOSTDAG proof-of-work protocol and maximum supply is about 28.7 billion KAS

PAXG.fact: each token represents one fine troy ounce of gold held in London vaults

STX.fact: blocks are anchored to Bitcoin through the Proof of Transfer mechanism
